 An event honoring veterans in Dubuque and the grand opening of a new museum in Galena, Ill., highlight the lineup of free events in the tri-state area this week.
 The Telegraph Herald continues to showcase no-cost community events in the area over the next seven days. Enjoy these local offerings without dipping into your bank account. Do you know of upcoming free events that should be featured in this space? Email Executive Editor Amy Gilligan at amy.gilligan@thmedia.com .

 Free offering spotlight
 Two community conversations in Dubuque County will highlight connections between environmental risk factors and Iowa’s cancer rates. The free events will be held today (Monday). 
 The first will be at 12:30 p.m. at James Kennedy Public Library, 320 First Ave. E. in Dyersville, Iowa, while the second will be at 5:30 p.m. at the Jackaline Baldwin Dunlap Technology Center Auditorium at the University of Dubuque, 1200 McCormick St. The events are a collaboration among Iowa Environmental Council, Dubuque County Public Health, Dubuque County Watersheds and Iowa Farmers Union. The topics will include pesticides, PFAS and nitrates, radon and Dubuque County’s cancer rates. Registration for the events is encouraged but not required. More information can be found at facebook.com/dubuquecountypublichealth .
 Veterans Day
 Local residents can mark Veterans Day this week in Dubuque by celebrating and honoring those who have served. 
 The annual American Legion Post 6 Veterans Day Ceremony will be held at 10:30 a.m. Wednesday, Nov. 11, at ImOn Arena, 1800 Admiral Sheehy Drive. 
 The ceremony honors all who have served in the U.S. military and will feature a guest speaker, as well as the East Dubuque Drum and Bugle Corps and the Dubuque Fire Pipe and Drums. All then are invited to a chili luncheon at 11:30 a.m. at the American Legion Club House, 1306 Delhi St.
